title: Activities
text:
Activities
  Meetings and scientific sessions organised by the group, most recent first.



  

    
      2–5 Sept2026
      
        Under way
        Four sessions at the XLII SEIO Congress
        Universidade de Santiago de Compostela
        The group organises four sessions at the 42nd National Congress on Statistics, Operations Research and Data Science.
      
    

    
      4–5 June2026
      
        II International Workshop on Bayesian Statistics
        CUNEF Universidad, Madrid
        A single-track meeting of seven keynote lectures and five contributed sessions, covering model selection, Bayesian computation, spatial and temporal modelling, financial econometrics, adversarial and robust machine learning, and applied Bayesian methods. Organised with CUNEF Universidad and funded by SEIO and CUNEF Universidad; registration was free of charge. The closing session announced the winner of the María Eugenia Castellanos Award.
        Workshop archiveProgrammeBook of abstractsVenue and committees
      
    

    
      17–18 June2024
      
        I International Workshop on Bayesian Statistics
        Universidad Carlos III de Madrid, Puerta de Toledo campus
        The first edition brought together 37 participants for 17 talks.
        
          Speakers and scientific committee
          
            Keynote speakers. Alan Gelfand (Duke University), Simon Wilson (Trinity College Dublin) and Miguel Ángel Gómez Villegas (Universidad Complutense de Madrid / Universidad CEU San Pablo).
            Invited speakers. María Eugenia Castellanos (Universidad Rey Juan Carlos), David Conesa (Universitat de València), Gonzalo García-Donato (Universidad de Castilla-La Mancha), Rosario Susi (Universidad Complutense de Madrid) and Pilar Gargallo (Universidad de Zaragoza).
            Scientific committee. Conchi Ausín, Stefano Cabras, Juanmi Díaz-Araque, Pepa Ramírez-Cobo and Mike Wiper.
          
        
        Original event page
      
    

    
      2023
      
        Three sessions at the XL SEIO Congress
        Elche
        Sessions on variable selection, on early-career research and on work by national and international researchers, the last including an invited contribution by Maria Kalli.
      
    

    
      2016
      
        Constitution of the working group
        XXXVI SEIO Congress, Toledo
        The group was constituted as a point of reference within SEIO for researchers working on Bayesian inference.
      
    

  



  
    Proposals
    
      Members may propose sessions at the SEIO congresses, workshops and other scientific activities. Write to roi.naveiro@cunef.edu or rsillero@us.es.

  Bayesian Working Group
  Grupo de Trabajo en Inferencia Bayesiana
  A working group of the Spanish Society of Statistics, Operations Research and Data Science (SEIO), constituted at the XXXVI SEIO Congress in Toledo in 2016.



  
    In brief
    
      Constituted2016, at the XXXVI SEIO Congress (Toledo)
      Parent societySociedad de Estadística e Investigación Operativa
      CoordinationRoi Naveiro (CUNEF Universidad) and M. Remedios Sillero-Denamiel (Universidad de Sevilla)
      BoardConcepción Ausín, Stefano Cabras, Gonzalo García-Donato, Pepa Ramírez-Cobo
      Contactroi.naveiro@cunef.edu · rsillero@us.es
    
  



  
    Purpose
    
      The stated aim of the group is to promote research in Bayesian inference and to disseminate its results among SEIO members, in the scientific community and in society at large.
      Its activity consists mainly of scientific sessions at the SEIO national congresses and of the International Workshop on Bayesian Statistics, held for the first time in 2024 and for the second in 2026. Sessions reserved for early-career researchers are a regular part of both.

            Thirty-seven participants and seventeen talks, with keynote lectures by Alan Gelfand, Simon Wilson and Miguel Ángel Gómez Villegas.
          
        
      
      All activities
    
  



  
    Membership
    
      Membership is open to SEIO members who work on or with Bayesian methods. To join the group, to correct an entry in the internal directory or to propose an activity, write to the coordinators at roi.naveiro@cunef.edu or rsillero@us.es.
      Membership of the Society itself is handled by SEIO.

title: II International Workshop on Bayesian Statistics
text:
2026 Workshop · Archive
  II International Workshop on Bayesian Statistics
  Madrid, 4–5 June 2026. Organised by the Bayesian Working Group of SEIO and CUNEF Universidad.



  
    In brief
    
      Dates4–5 June 2026
      VenueAula F1.2, LPC Campus, CUNEF Universidad, Madrid
      FormatSingle track: seven keynote lectures and five contributed sessions
      FundingSEIO and CUNEF Universidad; registration was free of charge
      Preceded byI International Workshop on Bayesian Statistics, Madrid, 2024
    
  



  
    Scope
    
      The second edition of the workshop followed the first, held in 2024 at Universidad Carlos III de Madrid. The programme combined seven keynote lectures with contributed sessions on model selection, Bayesian computation, spatial and temporal modelling, financial econometrics, adversarial and robust machine learning, and applied Bayesian methods. Several sessions were reserved for early-career researchers.
    
  



  
    Keynote lectures
    
      Peter MüllerThe University of Texas at AustinA semi-parametric Bayesian GLM and applications to outcome dependent sampling
      David RossellUniversitat Pompeu FabraHigh-dimensional model selection: transfer learning and projected computation
      Stefano CabrasUniversidad Carlos III de MadridObjective Bayesian Model Uncertainty Quantification under Missing Data
      Sylvia Frühwirth-SchnatterWU WienSparse Bayesian Factor Analysis for Gaussian and non-Gaussian Data
      María Dolores UgarteUniversidad Pública de NavarraOn smoothing risk patterns in areal data
      José Miguel Hernández-LobatoUniversity of CambridgeAdvances in Scalable Gaussian Processes
      Daniel Hernández-LobatoUniversidad Autónoma de MadridJoint entropy search for multi-objective Bayesian optimization with constraints and multiple fidelities
